clue.text: Quiet at the back, Roger!

parts.note: SH is the noise you make to hush someone
aft is the nautical word for towards the stern

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a teacher hushing the back row, and 'Roger!' arrives looking like radio confirmation rather than a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are coarse slang verbs for having sex with someone, and shaft has since widened into the sense of doing a person down.

clue.text: Film part of Black Narcissus?

definitions.meaning: the verb a director uses when capturing a scene on camera, filming it in the technical sense
the title names a flower; new growth that a plant like a narcissus sends up has a specific botanical name for it

explanation.walkthrough: Black Narcissus is a 1947 film, so the italic title looks like the whole point of the clue; the plant hiding inside it is what the second definition wants.
explanation.definitionFit: To film is to shoot, and a shoot is also the new growth on a plant such as a narcissus — two unrelated senses of one word.

clue.text: An experienced martial artist can flay you slowly

parts.note: the clue's opening word, taken as it stands
a dan is a black-belt grade, so its holder is a dan
a can is a tin
yOu skinned of its outside letters

explanation.walkthrough: A dan is the black-belt grade, so an experienced martial artist is a DAN; and 'flay', to take the skin off, is a neat way of saying strip a word's outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Andantino is a tempo marking a shade brisker than andante but still unhurried, so 'slowly' names the pace it asks a player for.

clue.text: One's filled with food yet goes around snaffling bread

indicators.note: to snaffle is to grab or pinch, so the turned word takes the next piece inside it
the word turns around, so it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: Something stuffed with food still makes the rounds, pinching bread as it goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes around' turns YET into TEY, which is 'snaffling' ROLL. The definition reads 'One is filled with food'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trolley is a wheeled cart, such as a food or drinks trolley on a train, loaded with refreshments.

clue.text: Queen with palace close to Ebbsfleet or Barking

parts.note: anagram fodder
the last letter of EbbsfleeT
the word 'or' joins the fodder whole

explanation.walkthrough: Ebbsfleet and Barking are both places on the London map, so the shuffling instruction sits camouflaged in the geography; barking = mad is the sense wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra was the last ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt, so 'Queen' defines her by example — one named monarch standing in for the general title.

clue.text: People love getting shot by him

definitions.meaning: the surface reading is gunfire, which nobody could love — that jar is the joke
the archer meant here fires arrows that cause love, so his victims welcome the wound

explanation.walkthrough: Cupid is the Roman god of love, drawn as a winged boy with a bow, and everything his arrow hits falls in love. There is no wordplay to find.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue defines him: he is the one archer whose targets want to be hit, and 'love' names both the feeling and what he deals in.

clue.text: Vote for Hull ensemble's lead conductor

parts.note: to vote for someone is to elect them
Rod Hull, the comedian with the emu, supplies the missing first name
the leading letter of Ensemble

explanation.walkthrough: A surname asking for its owner's first name is a standard Independent trick. Meanwhile the surface offers a Yorkshire choir and 'conductor' of the musical sort.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is the terminal carrying current into or out of a cell, so 'conductor' is meant electrically, not orchestrally.

clue.text: Film old northerner with uniform on

parts.note: the Picts were the ancient people of northern Britain
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet
re means on, as in a memo on expenses

explanation.walkthrough: Two abbreviations worth banking for good: U is 'uniform' in the NATO alphabet, and RE is the crossword's usual 'on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Picture is the trade's older word for a cinema film — going to the pictures — so it is a plain synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Sort out one's trunks

parts.note: anagram fodder
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a packing instruction for a beach holiday. 'Trunks' means bodies here, and TORSI is the Italian plural galleries prefer to torsos.
explanation.definitionFit: A torso is the trunk of the human body, and TORSI is its Italian-style plural, the form sculpture catalogues use.

clue.text: Lack of balance in upcoming TV awards defended by a judge

indicators.note: to be defended by something is to be guarded on both sides by it, so the awards sit inside the a and the judge

parts.note: to try a case is to judge it

indicators.note: in a down clue upcoming means rising, so the awards are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Emmys are the American television awards

explanation.surface: An imbalance in this year's TV awards is being defended by a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upcoming' reads the awards bottom to top; to try a case is to judge it.
explanation.definitionFit: Asymmetry is the absence of symmetry, an unevenness or imbalance between two sides.

clue.text: Unlikely double act formed when poodle dances with short duck

parts.note: anagram fodder
DUCK docked of its last letter

explanation.walkthrough: The Odd Couple is Neil Simon's play about two mismatched flatmates. A poodle dancing with a duck is itself an improbable pairing, which is the setter's joke.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd couple is any pair whose partnership looks improbable — the phrase Simon's title put into the language, and it fits a comic duo neatly.

clue.text: Bear in horror film released from trap

parts.note: Carrie, the Stephen King horror film

explanation.walkthrough: Your trap is your mouth, so what is released from it is speech — the setter's roundabout way of saying 'spoken'. The film supplies the sound, not the spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry a burden and to bear one are the same act; 'bear' is simply the more formal verb for lifting and conveying something.

clue.text: Confused old German director's on set at last

parts.note: the last letter of seT
the Angles were a Germanic tribe, from Angeln
d is the standard abbreviation for director

explanation.walkthrough: The Angles were a Germanic people before they were English, which is what 'old German' points at; and in an across clue 'on' puts a piece after the one it names.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangled means knotted together, and a tangled story or tangled thinking is a confused one — the figurative sense the definition uses.

clue.text: Travel to ancient city with one manuscript from the East

parts.note: MS, the shortening of manuscript, coming the other way
one is the Roman numeral I
Ur of the Chaldees, the crossword's default ancient city
the preposition, taken as it stands

explanation.walkthrough: UR and MS are both worth banking: the standard ancient city and the standard manuscript. An across entry running from the east is one read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourism is travel undertaken for pleasure, the abstract noun for the whole activity, which is how the definition uses 'travel' as a noun.

clue.text: A film screened by Bluebird's generating goodwill

parts.note: the clue's own 'A' leads off
Bluebird set this puzzle, so the setter's = my
It is a film title, and a two-letter one

explanation.walkthrough: Bluebird is this puzzle's setter, so 'Bluebird's' is simply MY — a setter pointing at themselves is standard practice. 'Screened' covers both showing a film and hiding something.
explanation.definitionFit: Amity is friendly relations between people or nations, so 'goodwill' is its plain synonym: the settled feeling rather than any single kind act.

clue.text: Wild boar turned quieter in garden

parts.note: BOAR with its letters loose
MUTER, meaning quieter, written backwards

explanation.walkthrough: The step that hides this one is hearing 'quieter' as the comparative MUTER, a word nobody says out loud. Boar and garden keep the surface rural.
explanation.definitionFit: An arboretum is a garden planted as a living collection of trees, so 'garden' names the wider class it belongs to.

clue.text: One month camping following a repayment

parts.note: the clue's 'a', which everything else follows
camping means under canvas, so a TENT, prised open as T...ENT
the word 'one' goes in whole
m is the standard abbreviation for month

explanation.walkthrough: Camping puts you in a tent, and this tent is opened up to hold what goes inside it. The answer's own history is worth knowing: at-one-ment, being made one again.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonement is making amends for a wrong, paying it back in effect, so 'repayment' names the settling of a moral debt rather than a financial one.

clue.text: Divorced blokes finally get Penthouse?

parts.note: a divorced couple live apart
blokes are men
the last letter of geT

explanation.walkthrough: 'Divorced' looks like an instruction to split something up and is really just a synonym, which is the main misdirection here. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A penthouse is the flat on the top floor of a block, so it defines the answer by example: one particular kind standing for the whole.

clue.text: Dotty, Brody and Nye discovered going after Eve, Tom, Dick and Harry

indicators.note: the rest of the letters go after the name Eve, so it comes first

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: dotty means crazy, so the letters of Brody are jumbled
discovered here means with its cover taken off, so the outer letters of Nye go, leaving its middle

parts.note: taken as written before it is uncovered

explanation.surface: A roll-call of people, Dotty, Brody and Nye, turning up after Eve, Tom, Dick and Harry.
explanation.walkthrough: The list of names makes 'Dotty' look like one more person; it is the anagram signal. The last three names are the definition, not part of the list.
explanation.definitionFit: Every Tom, Dick and Harry is an idiom for ordinary people in general, that is, all and sundry.

clue.text: Surprising announcement by King worried about revolutionary record label

parts.note: boo is what you say to make someone jump
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns right round, so the record is read backwards

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record
ate means worried about, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: A king, fretting over a radical album, makes a startling statement.
explanation.walkthrough: BOO and K, then 'revolutionary' turns LP into PL, followed by ATE (worried about).
explanation.definitionFit: A bookplate is a decorative label pasted inside a book's cover to show who owns it.

clue.text: Just over half of paratroopers punished proportionately

indicators.note: something punished is knocked about, so those seven letters are rearranged
the word has twelve letters, and just over half of it is its first seven

parts.note: taken as written before it is cut

explanation.surface: More than half of a parachute unit were disciplined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just over half of' keeps PARATRO, the first seven of twelve letters, and 'punished' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro rata is Latin for in proportion, used of payments shared out according to each person's share.

clue.text: E key fixed by guy primarily interested in computers?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the first letter of guy is taken

parts.note: taken as written; only its first letter is used

indicators.note: fixed in the sense of repaired or adjusted, so the letters of E key are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man who mainly likes computers mends the E key on his keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' gives G from guy, and 'fixed' turns E KEY into EEKY.
explanation.definitionFit: A geek is a person obsessed with technology, so geeky describes someone keen on computers, as the question mark allows.

clue.text: Universal Soldier

definitions.meaning: applying to everyone, without exception, rather than to one particular case
the most senior rank a top army officer can hold

explanation.walkthrough: Two words, two definitions and no wordplay whatever. The italics make the pair read as a film title, which is exactly what hides the split between them.
explanation.definitionFit: General means applying to everyone, hence 'universal'; and a general is an army's most senior officer, which makes 'soldier' a definition by example.

clue.text: Hastily release Lulu single after group experiences regular losses

parts.note: gRoUp keeping only its even letters
Shout was Lulu's breakthrough hit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular losses' is worth learning as an instruction to drop every other letter. Lulu's 'Shout' supplies the rest, and 'release' pretends to belong to the record too.
explanation.definitionFit: To rush out a record or a statement is to put it out in a hurry, which is what 'hastily release' spells out in full.

clue.text: Determined boy conceals alien

parts.note: a boy is somebody's son
ET is the crossword's standard alien

explanation.walkthrough: ET for 'alien' is one of the most-used shorthands in cryptics, and 'boy' nearly always wants SON or a short first name.
explanation.definitionFit: To be set on something is to have your mind fixed on doing it, so 'determined' is the phrase's ordinary adjectival sense.

clue.text: Anyone getting aggravated and dead angry

parts.note: anagram fodder
d. is the standard abbreviation for died

explanation.walkthrough: 'Aggravated' is the shuffling instruction and very nearly the definition as well, which is the setter having it both ways in one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoyed and angry name the same irritation at different strengths, annoyed sitting at the milder end of the scale.

clue.text: Poet with a bare head is depressed

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, is pushed down to the bottom of this down answer

parts.note: bare means nude, unclothed

explanation.surface: A poet who has gone bald is feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bare head' looks like baldness, but 'bare' is NUDE, and 'head is depressed' sends its N to the foot, giving UDEN after A.
explanation.definitionFit: W. H. Auden was the Anglo-American poet of Funeral Blues and September 1, 1939.

clue.text: One who eats at home, embarrassed to go about outside

indicators.note: the turned word sits outside, around the other piece
to go about is to turn round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: embarrassed people go red in the face
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A person eating at home is too embarrassed to go out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go about outside' sounds like leaving the house; it turns RED into DER, which sits 'outside' IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A diner is a person having a meal, especially in a restaurant, so someone eating.

clue.text: Lawrence emptied trawler — one fish!

parts.note: T. E. Lawrence, of Arabia, is the crossword's Lawrence
TrawleR emptied of everything between its ends
one = a, as in one moment or a moment

explanation.walkthrough: Lawrence of Arabia's initials do duty for the whole man all over cryptic crosswords, and 'emptied' hollows a word out to its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetra is a small tropical freshwater fish kept in home aquariums, so 'fish' defines it by its class.

clue.text: On the radio, setter had a clue type getting blanket coverage

parts.note: the setter is I, so this is 'I'd a'
clues come in two types, across and down

explanation.walkthrough: The setter is always 'I', which is the convention this depends on; and down is both a direction in the grid and the feathers the quilt is stuffed with.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt stuffed with eider duck feathers, so it really does provide blanket coverage — the newspaper phrase is the pun.

clue.text: Isle of Man Tourist Trophy area overrun by Chinese people

parts.note: the Isle of Man is MAN
the Han are China's majority people
the TT motorcycle races
a is the standard abbreviation for area

explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man really does host the Tourist Trophy, so the opening reads as one continuous place name — and only its first word belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Manhattan is an island between the Hudson and the East River, so 'Isle' is literal: the borough is land with water all round it.

clue.text: Film actor quietly leaving

parts.note: an actor is a player
p is piano, quietly, in music — and it is the letter that goes

explanation.walkthrough: P for 'quietly' is the piano marking off a sheet of music, one of the first abbreviations to learn. Here 'film' is the thin coating, nothing cinematic.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer is a thin sheet spread over a surface, the same sense as a film of dust or oil, rather than the cinema word.
